It separates, in its own text, the parts that vary by year from the parts that do not: subsection (a)(1)(A) fixes the three percentages and the rounding with no year term, while subparagraph (B) supplies a formula by which the dollar amounts are re-established for each calendar year. bendPointSet.quotedFormula: The PIA is the sum of three separate percentages of portions of average indexed monthly earnings. The portions depend on the year in which a worker attains age 62, becomes disabled before age 62, or dies before attaining age 62. For 2026 these portions are the first $1,286, the amount between $1,286 and $7,749, and the amount over $7,749. These dollar amounts are the "bend points" of the 2026 PIA formula.

percentageSource.quotedRule: (i) 90 percent of the individual’s average indexed monthly earnings (determined under subsection (b)) to the extent that such earnings do not exceed the amount established for purposes of this clause by subparagraph (B), (ii) 32 percent of the individual’s average indexed monthly earnings to the extent that such earnings exceed the amount established for purposes of clause (i) but do not exceed the amount established for purposes of this clause by subparagraph (B), and (iii) 15 percent of the individual’s average indexed monthly earnings to the extent that such earnings exceed the amount established for purposes of clause (ii)
percentageSource.statedFact: The three percentages are transcribed from the statute, which states them clause by clause and attaches each to the portion its own clause delimits. The bend-point DOLLAR amounts are transcribed instead from the 2026-dated formula page, because the statute does not print them: subparagraph (B) supplies only the formula by which they are re-established for each calendar year. That division is the publication's own, and it is why the percentages are structure and the bend points are year-scoped.

roundingRule.locator: Sec. 215(a)(1)(A) — the closing clause following clause (iii)
roundingRule.quotedRule: rounded, if not a multiple of $0.10, to the next lower multiple of $0.10, and thereafter increased as provided in subsection (i).
roundingRule.yearInvarianceBasis: The statute states this rounding in the closing clause of subsection (a)(1)(A) with no year term and with no re-establishment formula, in the same document whose subparagraph (a)(1)(B) supplies an explicit annual re-establishment formula for the bend-point dollar amounts and rounds THOSE to the nearest $1. That contrast is the publication's own: where a figure is meant to move with the year, this document says how it moves, and for the $0.10 truncation it says nothing of the kind.

indexingRule.locator: Indexing paragraphs preceding the "Earnings before and after indexing" table
indexingRule.quotedRule: A factor will always equal one for the year in which the person attains age 60 and all later years. The indexing factor for a prior year Y is the result of dividing the average wage index for the year in which the person attains age 60 by the average wage index for year Y. ... We use the highest 35 years of indexed earnings in a benefit computation. ... (The average is the result of dividing the sum of the 35 highest amounts by the number of months in 35 years.)

quotientRounding.locator: Sec. 215(e)(2) — Certain Wages And Self-Employment Income Not To Be Counted
quotientRounding.quotedRule: if an individual’s average indexed monthly earnings or, in the case of an individual whose primary insurance amount is computed under section 215(a) as in effect prior to January 1979, average monthly wage, computed under subsection (b) or for the purposes of subsection (d) is not a multiple of $1, it shall be reduced to the next lower multiple of $1.
quotientRounding.yearInvarianceBasis: The statute states this rounding in subsection (e)(2) with no year term and with no re-establishment formula, in the same document whose subparagraph (a)(1)(B) supplies an explicit annual re-establishment formula for the bend-point dollar amounts. That contrast is the publication's own: where a figure is meant to move with the year, this document says how it moves, and for subsection (e)(2) it says nothing of the kind.
quotientRounding.retrievalNote: This rule is NOT stated by the benefit-calculation page, which states the division and states no rounding for its result, and it is NOT stated by Sec. 215(b)(1), which defines the quotient and likewise states no rounding for it. It is stated by Sec. 215(e)(2), whose subject is the same quotient reached by a different subsection. An earlier transcription of this pack recorded the rule as unretrievable after reading only (b)(1); the rule was found on a later retrieval of the same statute in the implementing session and is transcribed here rather than inferred from the worked example.

declaredDomain.statedFact: The retrieved page presents the AWI series from 1985 through 2024; earlier years are shown on the page only as "[see data for prior years]" and were not retrieved. An earning year outside this domain refuses rather than being indexed by an adjacent year's factor.

fullRetirementAgeTable.locator: Table "Normal Retirement Age" — columns "Year of birth" and "Age"
fullRetirementAgeTable.yearInvarianceBasis: The publication names its own variation axis and names no other: "The table below shows how NRA varies by year of birth for retirees." Its terminal row is open-ended — "1960 and later | 67" — so the publication itself asserts the value for every birth year from 1960 forward rather than bounding the table to the year it was published. That open-ended terminal row is the in-document contrast: a table scoped to a publication year could not state a value for birth years later than its own publication.
fullRetirementAgeTable.applicabilityNote: The publication states: "Persons born on January 1 of any year should refer to the normal retirement age for the previous year." This model receives a birth YEAR and not a birth date, so it cannot apply that rule; a household born on January 1 must declare the previous year to obtain the age the publication assigns it.

declaredDomain.statedFact: The publication's first row is "1937 and prior" and its last row is "1960 and later", so the table declares a value for every birth year and its declared domain is open at both ends.

earlyReductionRule.quotedRule: In the case of early retirement, a benefit is reduced 5/9 of one percent for each month before normal retirement age, up to 36 months. If the number of months exceeds 36, then the benefit is further reduced 5/12 of one percent per month. For example, if the number of reduction months is 60 (the maximum number for retirement at 62 when normal retirement age is 67), then the benefit is reduced by 30 percent. This maximum reduction is calculated as 36 months times 5/9 of 1 percent plus 24 months times 5/12 of 1 percent.
earlyReductionRule.yearInvarianceBasis: The publication states the rule in its own prose with no year qualifier whatsoever, and works its maximum case arithmetically from that same rule rather than reading it off a year-scoped table. The companion publication "Starting Your Retirement Benefits Early" supplies the in-document dating contrast: its table is keyed by year of birth and its terminal row is open-ended — "1960 and later | 67 | 60 | $700 | 30.00%" — so the publication itself states a reduction for every birth year from 1960 forward, which a rule scoped to a publication year could not do.
